Parley can now use a model server you run yourself. In Settings → LLM Provider there is a new provider, **Custom**, for anything that speaks the OpenAI chat API — vLLM, LM Studio, LiteLLM, Ollama on another machine, a company gateway. You give it a base URL, the model id exactly as the server names it, and an API key if the server wants one; many self-hosted servers do not, and the field says so rather than pretending a key is required.

**Test connection** is the part worth the release. Pointing an app at your own server means getting three things right at once, and until now every one of them failed the same way — during a meeting, as a generic provider error. The button runs one throwaway completion through the same code path the analysis uses and answers in a sentence that names the thing to fix: the host could not be reached, the key was rejected, the URL is probably missing its `/v1`, the server has no model by that name, or it did not reply within fifteen seconds.

Every place in the app that used to say "add an API key" when a provider was not ready now says what is actually missing. For a custom endpoint that is the URL or the model, not the key.

Nothing changes for the built-in providers. Base URLs are used exactly as typed, minus trailing slashes; Parley does not append `/v1` for you, because gateways disagree about where they mount the API and a rewritten URL turns a 404 into a mystery.

This release changes nothing on iOS or Android — the iPhone gets its own update, 1.13, alongside it.
